doc.title: Wayne Andre interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 7, 2002

chapter: Jaco Pastorius and the Japan tour
title: Jaco Pastorius's big band and his musicianship
summary: Andre describes the camaraderie of Jaco's band, Jaco's eccentricities and his gift for time.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Yeah I’ll never forget that band.
I’ll bet. Was that a scene or what? A different kind of Benny Goodman scene?

No it was totally different. I mean there was a lot of love between the musicians in that band. There was a lot of camaraderie. Benny had a lot of musicians kind of divided in the band too you know. There was a lot of love in the musicians and there was a lot of love for Jaco, it’s just that I mean Jaco was just Jaco. He was just a crazy person. I mean like Jaco took his bass threw it in a lake in Japan, and he did it so the Japanese people would go diving for it and get it back. That’s how much vanity he had. And he’d walk around the bullet train — I’m talking dark things, negative things about him. Musically he was a genius. I mean musically, the thing that amazed me about Jaco was the only other person I ever saw that could lose one like he could was Bob Brookmeyer but he could lose one and boy he’d just know where one is all the time. Randy Brecker can too, and Michael, but not many players I know can really lose one and know exactly where it is. You know what I mean by that?
Not be playing over the bar line kind of.
